level: Cultivation Technician I / entry occupational pathway
intendedAudience: Learners progressing through the THC Cultivation Technician I pathway
Entry-level cultivation employees developing supervised operational competency
evidencePolicy: Use canonical evidence-backed science and operational references for durable principles. Facility SOPs, product labels, equipment manuals, and jurisdiction-specific requirements control when they are more specific. Reused curriculum modules are development dependencies and do not substitute for course-specific occupational review.
assessmentPolicy: This draft course is not credential evidence merely because its structure exists. Course-specific formative work, a course-level summative assessment, accessibility review, human technical review, and any required practical evidence must be completed and validated before the course can advance beyond draft/review status.
title: Integrated Cultivation Technician Practice Lab
description: Provides the integrated Technician I practice and capstone-preparation lab spanning shift prioritization, safety, sanitation, crop/environment observation, pH/EC and irrigation work, IPM scouting, propagation/canopy execution, harvest/postharvest traceability, dynamic-event response, records and handoff. The dedicated lab module now exists, but credential evidence remains development-only until practical, pilot, evaluator, accessibility, standard-setting and release gates are satisfied.
learningOutcomes: Prioritize an integrated cultivation shift from the supplied handoff, work orders, hazards, crop timing and authorization boundaries, identifying work that must stop, proceed, wait or be clarified.
Execute safe room entry, sanitation, crop observation and environmental evidence collection while preserving biosecurity, measurement context and stop-work boundaries.

Execute an assigned water and irrigation station using verified work-order identity, pH/EC measurement context, delivery checks and actual-versus-planned records without unsupported diagnosis or unauthorized correction.
Integrate IPM scouting with propagation or canopy work while protecting sanitation, material identity, evidence quality and treatment-selection authority boundaries.
Execute an authorized harvest-to-postharvest transition while preserving genealogy, quantity reconciliation, contamination holds, receiving status and material-location records.
Respond to an unexpected shift event, preserve unresolved evidence, escalate within role boundaries, reconcile the shift record and produce a handoff another qualified person can reconstruct.
